31-## Rule-coverability judgement (candid; I did not implement any rule)
32-
33-- Intersection and Omit/Pick wrapper (shadcn): the declared shape is trivial to parse. A rule would resolve each member, apply Omit/Pick as a key filter and union the members. The blocker is that the member types live in `react-aria-components` d.ts, so a rule needs package/d.ts resolution. Uncovered by inspection: whether those d.ts use only plain interface heritage (then a deterministic walker is enough) or `GlobalDOMAttributes<T>`-style generics over `@types/react`. I only know the parent names, not their definitions. About 100% of these missing props have a node_modules parent. Risk: Omit keys given as unions/aliases, class names mismatched.
34-- Interface extends (Spectrum): a rule would walk heritage across workspace packages (`@react-types/shared`, `react-aria`) and flatten, applying `Omit<X,'k'>` as a filter. Two of its inputs are not plain: `PossibleLinkDOMRenderProps<'div', R>` looks conditional on the tag, and `GlobalDOMAttributes<HTMLDivElement>` is generic. Plain heritage (`LinkDOMProps`, `HoverEvents`, `PressEvents`) is rule-coverable given workspace resolution. The structural side listed 1 prop of 102 for ListBoxItem, so heritage across modules is currently not flattened. Likely partial coverage: most of the 100 props come from the plain interfaces and the DOM event set; the conditional alias is the uncertain part.
35-- `ComponentProps<typeof X>`: if X is local or a workspace/aliased file (shadcn: 9 local, 20 `@/registry/...` aliases), rule = resolve X to its function, take its first param type, recurse. That needs tsconfig `paths`. If X comes from node_modules (`react-aria-components` 28, `cmdk` 21, `radix-ui`, `react-day-picker`; fixtures: `@chakra-ui/react` 706 of 706) the rule needs the d.ts, and for Chakra the 429163 `SystemProperties` + 71500 `Conditions` props come from generated mapped/conditional types. That bucket needs type evaluation unless the owner accepts a fixed lookup table of Chakra's style-prop names (about 845 names per recipe) keyed on the package version. Fragile, and I have no evidence the set is stable across components.
36-- Other / generic named type from a package: same as above; plus type-argument substitution for `X<T>` (generic default `T = object` is likely irrelevant to prop names, a cheap assumption I did not verify). Namespace imports (`ResizablePrimitive.PanelProps`) need namespace resolution.
37:- Factory (Chakra): `chakra("div", {variants})` is rule-coverable from the call arguments. The 13 missing props are `ref` (added by the factory) and variant keys (`inline`, `placement`), but evidence is 3 components, so the rule is only supported on small samples. Spectrum `createLeafComponent('x', function(props: P, ref, item){})`: coverable by reading the first function parameter, then it falls into the extends bucket. Two Spectrum initializers (as-expression, a nested call) were not unwrapped by my classifier either.
38:- Highest-value order by missing props: intersection (2932), extends (1874), ComponentProps (1427 + 506621 in the fixtures), other (1050), generic (831). None of the five is rule-coverable without module/package resolution; only the factory bucket (4%) is covered by the call arguments alone. Within real corpora, roughly the Spectrum 22% and the local-alias part of ComponentProps are coverable with workspace resolution; the node_modules-parented shadcn losses (and the Chakra fixtures) need the checker or a bundled type-declaration reader.
39-
40-## Caveats
41-
42-- Classification is syntax-only plus resolution through same-file declarations and relative imports; path aliases (`@/...`) and workspace packages are not resolved, which is why several shapes read "external". Top-shape bucket uses that resolution; tags are best-effort.
43-- Default `--collapse-inherited-props` was used (as asked), not `none`.
44-- The reverse direction (struct-only props; e.g. Chakra struct lists 1118 props vs checker 845 on Center) was not analysed.
45-- Missing-prop names for a few examples are limited to the first 5-8 listed above.
46-- A first accidental build ran with the default toolchain into the worktree `target/` dir (ignored by git) before the proper one; that dir is unused.
47-
48-## Appendix: per-corpus counts
49-
50:- chakra-ui (packages/react/src): 629 checker components, 629 structural, 11 with missing props, 13 missing props. Buckets 1-10: 11. All `factory` (chakra("tag",...)).
51-- mantine: 348 / 348, 0 missing.
52-- ant-design (components): 254 / 254, 0 missing.
53:- react-spectrum (packages): 1415 / 1415, 34 with missing, 2216 props. Buckets 1-10: 7, 11-100: 26, 101-1000: 1. Extends 24 (1874), factory 4 (322), plain 4 (5), other 2 (15).
54-- shadcn-ui (apps/v4): 1901 / 1901, 154 with missing, 6228 props. Buckets 1-10: 57, 11-100: 97. Intersection 54 (2932), componentprops 51 (1427), other 31 (1035), generic 15 (831), wrapper 3 (3).
55-- checker-default/chakra-only: 788 / 788, 707 with missing, 507327 props. Buckets 1-10: 82, 11-100: 17, 101-1000: 608. ComponentProps 706 (506621), intersection 1 (706).
56-- gate-large: 938 / 938, 770 with missing, 508163 props. Buckets 1-10: 111, 11-100: 51, 101-1000: 608. ComponentProps 769 (507457), intersection 1 (706).
57-- Runs: all exit 0. Peak RSS: chakra checker 6456 MB, gate-large 871, antd 886, shadcn 856, spectrum 732, others under 1 GB or unsampled.

28-- Wrapper (Omit/Pick/Partial) as top shape: 3 shadcn components, 3 props (AlertDialogTitle, DialogTitle, SheetTitle: `tw`).
29-- Mapped, conditional, indexed, recipe, polymorphic as top shape: 0 components.
30-
31-## Rule-coverability judgement (candid; I did not implement any rule)
32-
33-- Intersection and Omit/Pick wrapper (shadcn): the declared shape is trivial to parse. A rule would resolve each member, apply Omit/Pick as a key filter and union the members. The blocker is that the member types live in `react-aria-components` d.ts, so a rule needs package/d.ts resolution. Uncovered by inspection: whether those d.ts use only plain interface heritage (then a deterministic walker is enough) or `GlobalDOMAttributes<T>`-style generics over `@types/react`. I only know the parent names, not their definitions. About 100% of these missing props have a node_modules parent. Risk: Omit keys given as unions/aliases, class names mismatched.
34-- Interface extends (Spectrum): a rule would walk heritage across workspace packages (`@react-types/shared`, `react-aria`) and flatten, applying `Omit<X,'k'>` as a filter. Two of its inputs are not plain: `PossibleLinkDOMRenderProps<'div', R>` looks conditional on the tag, and `GlobalDOMAttributes<HTMLDivElement>` is generic. Plain heritage (`LinkDOMProps`, `HoverEvents`, `PressEvents`) is rule-coverable given workspace resolution. The structural side listed 1 prop of 102 for ListBoxItem, so heritage across modules is currently not flattened. Likely partial coverage: most of the 100 props come from the plain interfaces and the DOM event set; the conditional alias is the uncertain part.
35-- `ComponentProps<typeof X>`: if X is local or a workspace/aliased file (shadcn: 9 local, 20 `@/registry/...` aliases), rule = resolve X to its function, take its first param type, recurse. That needs tsconfig `paths`. If X comes from node_modules (`react-aria-components` 28, `cmdk` 21, `radix-ui`, `react-day-picker`; fixtures: `@chakra-ui/react` 706 of 706) the rule needs the d.ts, and for Chakra the 429163 `SystemProperties` + 71500 `Conditions` props come from generated mapped/conditional types. That bucket needs type evaluation unless the owner accepts a fixed lookup table of Chakra's style-prop names (about 845 names per recipe) keyed on the package version. Fragile, and I have no evidence the set is stable across components.
36-- Other / generic named type from a package: same as above; plus type-argument substitution for `X<T>` (generic default `T = object` is likely irrelevant to prop names, a cheap assumption I did not verify). Namespace imports (`ResizablePrimitive.PanelProps`) need namespace resolution.
37:- Factory (Chakra): `chakra("div", {variants})` is rule-coverable from the call arguments. The 13 missing props are `ref` (added by the factory) and variant keys (`inline`, `placement`), but evidence is 3 components, so the rule is only supported on small samples. Spectrum `createLeafComponent('x', function(props: P, ref, item){})`: coverable by reading the first function parameter, then it falls into the extends bucket. Two Spectrum initializers (as-expression, a nested call) were not unwrapped by my classifier either.
38:- Highest-value order by missing props: intersection (2932), extends (1874), ComponentProps (1427 + 506621 in the fixtures), other (1050), generic (831). None of the five is rule-coverable without module/package resolution; only the factory bucket (4%) is covered by the call arguments alone. Within real corpora, roughly the Spectrum 22% and the local-alias part of ComponentProps are coverable with workspace resolution; the node_modules-parented shadcn losses (and the Chakra fixtures) need the checker or a bundled type-declaration reader.
39-
40-## Caveats
41-
42-- Classification is syntax-only plus resolution through same-file declarations and relative imports; path aliases (`@/...`) and workspace packages are not resolved, which is why several shapes read "external". Top-shape bucket uses that resolution; tags are best-effort.
43-- Default `--collapse-inherited-props` was used (as asked), not `none`.
44-- The reverse direction (struct-only props; e.g. Chakra struct lists 1118 props vs checker 845 on Center) was not analysed.
45-- Missing-prop names for a few examples are limited to the first 5-8 listed above.
46-- A first accidental build ran with the default toolchain into the worktree `target/` dir (ignored by git) before the proper one; that dir is unused.

"""Compare structural (--no-checker) vs checker extraction per component and prop.

Usage: python3 -I diffmap.py <name>   (reads <name>.checker.json / <name>.struct.json here)
Writes <name>.diff.json with every per-prop classification.
"""
import json, sys, os
from collections import Counter

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
UNRES = {'opaque', 'truncated', 'unknown', 'any'}


def load(path):
    d = json.load(open(path))
    d.pop('stats', None)
    return d


def comp_props(d, c):
    """name -> (type, origin) for a component: own props plus inherited members."""
    out = {}
    for sid in c['props']:
        for n, pid in d['propSets'][sid].items():
            p = d['props'][pid]
            out[n] = (p['type'], 'own', p)
    for inh in c['inheritance']:
        m = d['propSets'].get(inh['members']) if inh.get('members') else None
        for n, pid in (m or {}).items():
            if n not in out:
                p = d['props'][pid]
                out[n] = (p['type'], 'inherited', p)
    return out


def kinds(t, acc=None):
    acc = set() if acc is None else acc
    if isinstance(t, dict):
        if 'kind' in t:
            acc.add(t['kind'])
        for v in t.values():
            kinds(v, acc)
    elif isinstance(t, list):
        for v in t:
            kinds(v, acc)
    return acc


def norm(t):
    if isinstance(t, dict):
        t = {k: norm(v) for k, v in t.items()}
        if t.get('kind') == 'literalUnion':
            t = {'kind': 'union', 'members': [{'kind': 'stringLiteral', 'value': m} for m in t.get('members', [])]}
        if t.get('kind') == 'union' and isinstance(t.get('members'), list):
            t['members'] = sorted(t['members'], key=lambda m: json.dumps(m, sort_keys=True))
        return t
    if isinstance(t, list):
        return [norm(v) for v in t]
    return t


def classify(s, c):
    if s == c or norm(s) == norm(c):
        return 'equal'
    if s.get('kind') in ('elementType', 'ref') and c.get('kind') in ('union', 'named', 'stringLiteral'):
        return 'spelled_differently'
    sk, ck = kinds(s), kinds(c)
    top = s.get('kind')
    # unresolved: the structural answer holds an opaque/unknown/any/truncated or an unexpanded
    # named reference where the checker has something else
    if top in UNRES or top == 'named' or (sk & {'opaque'} and not ck & {'opaque'}):
        if not (ck & {'opaque'} and top == 'opaque'):
            return 'struct_unresolved'
    if ck & {'opaque'} and not (sk & {'opaque'}):
        return 'checker_opaque_struct_concrete'
    return 'concrete_different'


def main(name):
    ch = load(f'{HERE}/{name}.checker.json')
    st = load(f'{HERE}/{name}.struct.json')
    res = []
    comp_cls = Counter()
    only = Counter()
    for cn, cc in ch['components'].items():
        sc = st['components'].get(cn)
        if sc is None:
            only['component_only_checker'] += 1
            continue
        cp, sp = comp_props(ch, cc), comp_props(st, sc)
        worst = 'equal'
        order = ['equal', 'spelled_differently', 'concrete_different', 'checker_opaque_struct_concrete', 'struct_unresolved', 'only']
        for pn in set(cp) | set(sp):
            if pn not in cp or pn not in sp:
                cls = 'only_checker' if pn in cp else 'only_struct'
                origin = (cp.get(pn) or sp.get(pn))[1]
                res.append(dict(c=cn, p=pn, cls=cls, origin=origin))
                worst = 'only'
                continue
            ct, origin, cprop = cp[pn]
            stt, _, sprop = sp[pn]
            cls = classify(stt, ct)
            if cls != 'equal':
                res.append(dict(c=cn, p=pn, cls=cls, origin=origin, s=stt, k=ct,
                                parent=(cprop.get('parent') or {}).get('name'),
                                file=(cprop.get('parent') or {}).get('fileName')))
            else:
                res.append(dict(c=cn, p=pn, cls='equal', origin=origin))
            if cls != 'equal' and order.index(cls) > order.index(worst):
                worst = cls
        comp_cls[worst] += 1
    for cn in st['components']:
        if cn not in ch['components']:
            only['component_only_struct'] += 1
    json.dump(dict(components=len(ch['components']), comp_cls=comp_cls, only=only, rows=res),
              open(f'{HERE}/{name}.diff.json', 'w'))
    pc = Counter((r['cls'], r['origin']) for r in res)
    tot = Counter(r['cls'] for r in res)

"""Compare structural (--no-checker) vs checker extraction per component and prop.

Usage: python3 -I diffmap.py <name>   (reads <name>.checker.json / <name>.struct.json here)
Writes <name>.diff.json with every per-prop classification.
"""
import json, sys, os
from collections import Counter

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
UNRES = {'opaque', 'truncated', 'unknown', 'any'}


def load(path):
    d = json.load(open(path))
    d.pop('stats', None)
    return d


def comp_props(d, c):
    """name -> (type, origin) for a component: own props plus inherited members."""
    out = {}
    for sid in c['props']:
        for n, pid in d['propSets'][sid].items():
            p = d['props'][pid]
            out[n] = (p['type'], 'own', p)
    for inh in c['inheritance']:
        m = d['propSets'].get(inh['members']) if inh.get('members') else None
        for n, pid in (m or {}).items():
            if n not in out:
                p = d['props'][pid]
                out[n] = (p['type'], 'inherited', p)
    return out


def kinds(t, acc=None):
    acc = set() if acc is None else acc
    if isinstance(t, dict):
        if 'kind' in t:
            acc.add(t['kind'])
        for v in t.values():
            kinds(v, acc)
    elif isinstance(t, list):
        for v in t:
            kinds(v, acc)
    return acc


def norm(t):
    if isinstance(t, dict):
        t = {k: norm(v) for k, v in t.items()}
        if t.get('kind') == 'literalUnion':
            t = {'kind': 'union', 'members': [{'kind': 'stringLiteral', 'value': m} for m in t.get('members', [])]}
        if t.get('kind') == 'union' and isinstance(t.get('members'), list):
            t['members'] = sorted(t['members'], key=lambda m: json.dumps(m, sort_keys=True))
        return t
    if isinstance(t, list):
        return [norm(v) for v in t]
    return t


def classify(s, c):
    if s == c or norm(s) == norm(c):
        return 'equal'
    if s.get('kind') in ('elementType', 'ref') and c.get('kind') in ('union', 'named', 'stringLiteral'):
        return 'spelled_differently'
    sk, ck = kinds(s), kinds(c)
    top = s.get('kind')
    # unresolved: the structural answer holds an opaque/unknown/any/truncated or an unexpanded
    # named reference where the checker has something else
    if top in UNRES or top == 'named' or (sk & {'opaque'} and not ck & {'opaque'}):
        if not (ck & {'opaque'} and top == 'opaque'):
            return 'struct_unresolved'
    if ck & {'opaque'} and not (sk & {'opaque'}):
        return 'checker_opaque_struct_concrete'
    return 'concrete_different'


def main(name):
    ch = load(f'{HERE}/{name}.checker.json')
    st = load(f'{HERE}/{name}.struct.json')
    res = []
    comp_cls = Counter()
    only = Counter()
    for cn, cc in ch['components'].items():
        sc = st['components'].get(cn)
        if sc is None:
            only['component_only_checker'] += 1
            continue
        cp, sp = comp_props(ch, cc), comp_props(st, sc)
        worst = 'equal'
        order = ['equal', 'spelled_differently', 'concrete_different', 'checker_opaque_struct_concrete', 'struct_unresolved', 'only']
        for pn in set(cp) | set(sp):
            if pn not in cp or pn not in sp:
                cls = 'only_checker' if pn in cp else 'only_struct'
                origin = (cp.get(pn) or sp.get(pn))[1]
                res.append(dict(c=cn, p=pn, cls=cls, origin=origin))
                worst = 'only'
                continue
            ct, origin, cprop = cp[pn]
            stt, _, sprop = sp[pn]
            cls = classify(stt, ct)
            if cls != 'equal':
                res.append(dict(c=cn, p=pn, cls=cls, origin=origin, s=stt, k=ct,
                                parent=(cprop.get('parent') or {}).get('name'),
                                file=(cprop.get('parent') or {}).get('fileName')))
            else:
                res.append(dict(c=cn, p=pn, cls='equal', origin=origin))
            if cls != 'equal' and order.index(cls) > order.index(worst):
                worst = cls
        comp_cls[worst] += 1
    for cn in st['components']:
        if cn not in ch['components']:
            only['component_only_struct'] += 1
    json.dump(dict(components=len(ch['components']), comp_cls=comp_cls, only=only, rows=res),
              open(f'{HERE}/{name}.diff.json', 'w'))
    pc = Counter((r['cls'], r['origin']) for r in res)
    tot = Counter(r['cls'] for r in res)
    print(name, 'components', len(ch['components']), 'struct', len(st['components']), dict(comp_cls), dict(only))
    print(' props total', len(res), dict(tot))
    print(' by origin', dict(pc))

"""Per-component props that only the checker lists.

Usage: python3 -I missing.py <corpus>   reads <corpus>.checker.json / .struct.json in this dir,
writes <corpus>.missing.json (components with >=1 missing prop) and prints bucket counts.
"""
import json, sys, os
from collections import Counter

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def comp_props(d, c):
    out = {}
    for sid in c['props']:
        for n, pid in d['propSets'][sid].items():
            out[n] = ('own', d['props'][pid])
    for inh in c['inheritance']:
        m = d['propSets'].get(inh['members']) if inh.get('members') else None
        for n, pid in (m or {}).items():
            if n not in out:
                out[n] = ('inherited', d['props'][pid])
    return out


def bucket(n):
    return '1-10' if n <= 10 else '11-100' if n <= 100 else '101-1000' if n <= 1000 else '1000+'


def main(name):
    ch = json.load(open(f'{HERE}/{name}.checker.json'))
    st = json.load(open(f'{HERE}/{name}.struct.json'))
    rows = []
    b = Counter()
    both = 0
    only_ck = 0
    for key, cc in ch['components'].items():
        sc = st['components'].get(key)
        if sc is None:
            only_ck += 1
            continue
        both += 1
        cp, sp = comp_props(ch, cc), comp_props(st, sc)
        miss = [n for n in cp if n not in sp]
        if not miss:
            continue
        ms = []
        for n in miss:
            o, p = cp[n]
            par = p.get('parent') or {}
            ms.append(dict(p=n, origin=o, parent=par.get('name'), pfile=par.get('fileName')))
        rows.append(dict(key=key, name=cc['displayName'], file=cc['filePath'], detectedBy=cc.get('detectedBy'),
                         n=len(miss), checkerTotal=len(cp), structTotal=len(sp), missing=ms))
        b[bucket(len(miss))] += 1
    json.dump(rows, open(f'{HERE}/{name}.missing.json', 'w'))
    print(name, 'checker comps', len(ch['components']), 'struct comps', len(st['components']), 'both', both,
          'onlyChecker', only_ck, 'withMissing', len(rows), 'missingSum', sum(r['n'] for r in rows), dict(b))


main(sys.argv[1])

"""Per-component props that only the checker lists.

Usage: python3 -I missing.py <corpus>   reads <corpus>.checker.json / .struct.json in this dir,
writes <corpus>.missing.json (components with >=1 missing prop) and prints bucket counts.
"""
import json, sys, os
from collections import Counter

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def comp_props(d, c):
    out = {}
    for sid in c['props']:
        for n, pid in d['propSets'][sid].items():
            out[n] = ('own', d['props'][pid])
    for inh in c['inheritance']:
        m = d['propSets'].get(inh['members']) if inh.get('members') else None
        for n, pid in (m or {}).items():
            if n not in out:
                out[n] = ('inherited', d['props'][pid])
    return out


def bucket(n):
    return '1-10' if n <= 10 else '11-100' if n <= 100 else '101-1000' if n <= 1000 else '1000+'


def main(name):
    ch = json.load(open(f'{HERE}/{name}.checker.json'))
    st = json.load(open(f'{HERE}/{name}.struct.json'))
    rows = []
    b = Counter()
    both = 0
    only_ck = 0
    for key, cc in ch['components'].items():
        sc = st['components'].get(key)
        if sc is None:
            only_ck += 1
            continue
        both += 1
        cp, sp = comp_props(ch, cc), comp_props(st, sc)
        miss = [n for n in cp if n not in sp]
        if not miss:
            continue
        ms = []
        for n in miss:
            o, p = cp[n]
            par = p.get('parent') or {}
            ms.append(dict(p=n, origin=o, parent=par.get('name'), pfile=par.get('fileName')))
        rows.append(dict(key=key, name=cc['displayName'], file=cc['filePath'], detectedBy=cc.get('detectedBy'),
                         n=len(miss), checkerTotal=len(cp), structTotal=len(sp), missing=ms))
        b[bucket(len(miss))] += 1
    json.dump(rows, open(f'{HERE}/{name}.missing.json', 'w'))
    print(name, 'checker comps', len(ch['components']), 'struct comps', len(st['components']), 'both', both,
          'onlyChecker', only_ck, 'withMissing', len(rows), 'missingSum', sum(r['n'] for r in rows), dict(b))


main(sys.argv[1])

#!/bin/bash
# one process at a time, 14 GB RSS watchdog
BIN=/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/target-census/release/caliper-docgen
C=/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/corpora
F=/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures
OUT=$F/shrink/census
LIMIT_KB=$((14*1024*1024))
run() { # name src mode flag
  name=$1; src=$2; mode=$3; flag=$4
  [ -d "$src" ] || { echo "$name $mode missing-src $src" >> $OUT/status.txt; return; }
  start=$(date +%s)
  $BIN extract --src "$src" --json --quiet --no-cache $flag > $OUT/$name.$mode.json 2> $OUT/$name.$mode.err &
  pid=$!
  peak=0; killed=0
  while kill -0 $pid 2>/dev/null; do
    rss=$(ps -o rss= -p $pid 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')
    [ -n "$rss" ] && [ "$rss" -gt "$peak" ] && peak=$rss
    if [ -n "$rss" ] && [ "$rss" -gt "$LIMIT_KB" ]; then kill -9 $pid; killed=1; fi
    sleep 1
  done
  wait $pid; code=$?
  echo "$name $mode exit=$code killed=$killed peakRSS_MB=$((peak/1024)) secs=$(( $(date +%s)-start ))" >> $OUT/status.txt
}
: > $OUT/status.txt
for spec in "gate-large|$F/gate-large/src" "chakra-only|$F/checker-default/chakra-only/src" "shadcn|$C/shadcn-ui/apps/v4" "antd|$C/ant-design/components" "mantine|$C/mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src" "spectrum|$C/react-spectrum/packages" "chakra|$C/chakra-ui/packages/react/src"; do
  n=${spec%%|*}; s=${spec#*|}
  run $n "$s" struct --no-checker
  run $n "$s" checker ""
done

---
cargo/caliper-docgen-core: minor
---

`ComponentMapping` and `SourceData` gain a crate-internal field each (what a component's body and the rest of its file write in JSX), so neither can be built with a struct expression outside the crate any more: use `ComponentMapping::new` and `SourceData::default()`. Extraction output is unchanged; the declaration cache schema moves to 39, so an existing cache is rebuilt once.
---
cargo/caliper-docgen-core: minor
cargo/caliper-docgen: minor
cargo/caliper-docgen-napi: minor
npm/caliper-docgen: minor
npm/caliper-docgen-storybook: minor
npm/caliper-docgen-napi: minor
npm/caliper-docgen-vite-plugin: minor
---

Large inherited sources are collapsed by default, wherever they are declared, and the checker's answer is collapsed the same way.

Breaking for the Storybook addon: its default output changes. `collapseInheritedProps` now defaults to `'dependencies'` instead of `'none'`, so an inherited source too large to be an API (a dependency's DOM, ARIA or style-system set of more than 30 props, or any source of more than 200 props) is one inheritance layer of names instead of hundreds of Controls rows. A component's own props and the notable inherited ones are still listed. The props inside such a layer get no Controls row, and a story's `args` naming one shows it as undocumented: that is intended, and a later release adds the props stories and call sites use. Set `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'` to list every inherited prop as before.

For every consumer, the default `dependencies` mode now also collapses a source in the project's own code that declares more than 200 props (a design system's style props, such as Chakra's `SystemProperties` in Chakra's own repository); before, only dependency sources collapsed. With the checker on, the props a collapsed layer names are no longer also listed from the checker's answer: the checker's props follow the structural answer's layers, so both give the same layers.
